data.narrative:
CubeFabs, a Series E semiconductor company founded by Matthew Putman (PhD, former Columbia materials science professor) and his father John, has raised approximately $182M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 3 public semiconductor companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in the chips and semiconductors sector, with 5 directly comparable private companies at Series D–F stage.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical for Series E advancement to the $182M raised proxy, implying a valuation of $255M. Peer-median analysis across 5 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—including Etched ($5.0B, Series E), Ayar Labs ($3.8B, Series E), Tenstorrent ($2.7B, Series D), SambaNova Systems ($11.0B, Series F), and Nearfield Instruments ($1.6B, Series D)—yields a median valuation of $3.8B, with a range of $1.6B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring using the semiconductor sector's 18.9x price-to-sales median cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $217M (floor) to $4.3B (ceiling), with a median of $2.0B. The substantial spread reflects stage and maturity variation within the peer set. Key uncertainties include CubeFabs's revenue trajectory relative to later-stage competitors and the timing of inflection toward profitability in an capital-intensive sector.
